observation.visible_scene: An overhead view of a pale pine panel lying flat on a white tabletop. Over the course of the clip two small rectangular wooden blocks, then two long wooden slats, are introduced and positioned on the panel by a pair of hands.
visible_changes: At the start only the bare panel is visible; two hands then carry in two small blocks from below and set them on the panel, one on the left third and one on the right third, roughly symmetric, after which the hands release and withdraw.

A long flat slat subsequently appears lying across the front (lower) edge of the panel, then is shifted backward and upward so that it rests on top of the two blocks, elevated above the panel surface; two hands grip its ends to hold and fine-tune this position before withdrawing.

A second, rounded-edge slat is then brought in from below by two hands and laid flat on the panel in front of (closer to the viewer than) the blocks; the hands keep holding its two ends and adjust it through the final frames.
Throughout, the panel and the two blocks remain at fixed positions; only the slats and hands move relative to them.
outside_clip_unknowns: What preceded frame 1 and what follows frame 41 (the second slat is still being held at the cut).
Whether any pieces are fastened together or merely resting, and the intended end product.
How the first slat was lifted onto the blocks in the frames where the hands are largely out of view.
uncertain_details: Minor apparent scaling/vertical drift of the panel across frames may be slight camera movement or hand-induced panel shift; the background gives no firm evidence either way.
The exact moment and agent that moved the first slat from the front edge to the block tops is partly obscured.
